images.title: The regrouping ladder
images.purpose: Recap the topic's method: each place regroups into 10 of the next smaller place, and the point enters the quotient at the first step.
images.composition: Four rounded place boxes in one horizontal row across the middle, joined by three curved arrows, with a single note above the first arrow; lots of white space above and below.
exact_structure: 4 rounded boxes in one row, left to right: Ones (teal #0072B2), Tenths (amber #E69F00), Hundredths (amber #E69F00), Thousandths (amber #E69F00).
3 curved grey #6B7280 arrows over the gaps, from each box to the next on its right, each labelled 1 = 10.
The first arrow, Ones to Tenths, is drawn thicker in reddish purple #CC79A7, with a large reddish purple dot (a decimal point) above it and the note point goes in here.
Bottom right, small: a green #009E73 tick next to the text check: multiply back.
rejection: more or fewer than 4 place boxes or 3 arrows
the boxes in any order other than Ones, Tenths, Hundredths, Thousandths
the highlighted arrow anywhere other than between Ones and Tenths
images.takeaway: Keep regrouping 1 into 10 of the next place until nothing is left, and put the point in when Ones become Tenths.
images.description: Four place boxes, Ones, Tenths, Hundredths and Thousandths, joined by arrows marked 1 = 10, with the first arrow highlighted where the decimal point goes in.
images.context: Shown beside the practice task on long division with decimals.
images.teaching_notes: Have students point to each arrow while saying what a leftover becomes in the next place.

image_decisions.why: A compact recap of the regrouping steps supports the practice task without giving any answers.
